q: Why paste one old real example of a document into the prompt?
options: To give the AI your office's exact format, vocabulary and house style
To make the AI reply faster
Because AI cannot write unless you paste something long
To check if the AI can remember the document
explanation: A generic prompt produces a generic document. Your old, accepted example carries the correct headings, order and tone, so the AI follows your format instead of guessing.

q: What does the template-extraction prompt produce?
options: A shorter summary of your document
A reusable fill-in version with slots like [DATE] and [RECIPIENT]
A list of spelling errors in the document
A new document on a different topic
explanation: It keeps the document's exact structure but replaces the specific details with marked fill-in slots. Every future document of that type can start from this template.

q: Which tone fits formal correspondence to a permanent secretary?
options: Warm: greetings and friendly phrasing
Concise: bullet points and a direct ask
Official: full phrases, no contractions
Casual: as if messaging a friend
explanation: Use the official tone for formal correspondence and regulators, concise for busy colleagues, and warm for customers, parents and community members.

q: Before pasting an old example that mentions named colleagues and salary figures, you should:
options: Paste it as it is, because it is your own document
Strip out other people's personal details and confidential figures first
Delete the whole document instead
Ask the AI for permission first
explanation: Even your own documents may contain other people's personal data or confidential figures. Remove them before pasting. The Day 2 privacy rules apply every day.
